The source file hash 9206b3d8...e557 matches Section 11.

H1 matches printed p. 147 ('When bias was present, the measure of bias was a negative value'), H2 printed p. 150 ('the true parameter value systematically fell above the CIs'), H3 printed p. 121 ('All power for MINT is near zero') and p. 148 ('never reached the .80 level'), H4 printed p. 150 ('Tentatively, a minimum sample size of 5000 ...'). All faithful.

SHOULD-FIX: Chen's own abstract (PDF p. 2) and Chapter 5 summary (printed p. 144) say 'Type I error rate and power for all five effects were either within the robustness criteria or reached the ideal range', which conflicts with her p. 148 MINT statement used as H3. The paper does not say that the source is inconsistent or why the Chapter 4-5 statement was chosen. The same passages claim that RDD CIs 'made opposite statistical significance conclusions compared to the RCT estimates'. That claim is not in the packet inventory, and it may be partly checkable from the printed Tables 4.6-4.7 estimates and SEs. Add it as a claim (or record why it is not assessable), and note the source's internal inconsistency on power.

BLOCKING: the E4 estimand is a raw rejection rate with 'positive means zero is excluded more often'. A rate cannot be negative, so 'same direction' is guaranteed and carries no information. The scientifically meaningful contrast is against the null (power minus nominal .05). Chen's value then becomes 0.063 - .05 = 0.013, which is within the stated .013 tolerance of zero; her Figure 4.28 values equal our rates with h set to 0 (0.0585, 0.0539, 0.0571 in results/digitized_rates.csv), and Section 4.3 itself calls her curve 'the shape of a Type I error curve'. The direction against ours (0.786) is therefore 'zero vs nonzero', not 'same'. The contract forbids raw parameters in place of a contrast against the null. Redefine E4 (e.g., rejection rate minus .05) with recomputed magnitude/direction, or justify the raw rate explicitly and label direction accordingly. Also align the Table 3 H3 'Same direction? yes' and the Introduction's 'MINT power point[s] the same way as hers'.

E1/E2 0.005 and E3 0.01 rounding bounds verified (two printed decimals, e.g. '12.50%', '24.10%' on source PDF pp. 102, 138; means keep 0.005; difference of two means sums to 0.01). E4 0.013 = mean reading error (0.0187, 0.0052, 0.0131) rounded up. The packet labels it kind 'prespecified', but it was derived from the digitizing, not fixed in advance; the page wording 'reading error of her figure' is accurate (polish: packet kind).
'Descriptive point estimates; not equivalence.' is present, and the MC SE (.007 per cell) is stated. E1-E3 magnitudes 'smaller' and E1 'zero vs nonzero' are correct.
